title: Systems with No Solution Core Test
description: Recognize systems whose lines are parallel and therefore have no ordered-pair solution.

questions.questionText: How many solutions does the system y = -3x - 5 and y = -3x + 1 have?
questions.explanation: The lines have the same slope but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never intersect.

questions.questionText: Why does y = 3x + 1 and y = 3x - 5 have no solution?
options: different slopes and the same y-intercept
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have equal slopes. Different y-intercepts mean they are distinct lines, so they do not meet.

questions.questionText: Elimination gives 0 = -1 for the system x + 2y = 5 and -2x - 4y = -11. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: A false statement like 0 = 1 means no ordered pair can satisfy both equations.

questions.questionText: Scale the first equation in -4x + 3y = -10 and 12x - 9y = 28 by -3, then subtract. Which result shows the system is inconsistent?
questions.explanation: After equivalent scaling, the variable terms match but the constants do not. Subtracting leaves a false statement.

questions.questionText: Which system has no solution?
questions.explanation: The no-solution system is the one with parallel lines: same slope, different intercepts.

questions.questionText: On a graph, what would the solution picture look like for y = 5x + 1 and y = 5x - 5?
options: a vertical line crossing a horizontal line
questions.explanation: A system has no solution when its two lines are parallel and distinct, so there is no intersection point.

questions.questionText: A student says y = x - 5 and y = x + 1 must share at least one point because both are lines. Is the student correct?
options: no; parallel lines do not share any ordered pair
yes; any two lines have exactly one solution
yes; the y-intercepts are both solutions
no; different slopes are required for no solution
questions.correctAnswer: no; parallel lines do not share any ordered pair
questions.explanation: Distinct parallel lines never intersect, so they do not share an ordered-pair solution.

questions.questionText: In 4x + y = 4 and -8x - 2y = -10, what algebraic sign points to no solution?
options: the coefficients and constants are all proportional
the coefficients are proportional, but the constants are not
questions.correctAnswer: the coefficients are proportional, but the constants are not
questions.explanation: Proportional variable coefficients with nonproportional constants describe parallel distinct lines.

questions.questionText: How is a system that simplifies to 0 = 0 different from y = 2x - 5 and y = 2x + 1?
questions.explanation: The statement 0 = 0 means the equations represent the same line. A no-solution system simplifies to a false statement.

questions.questionText: Two plans are modeled by y = -3x + 1 and y = -3x - 5. What context clue would match no solution?
options: one plan starts at zero and the other starts later
the exact same rate and starting value
the same rate but different starting values
questions.correctAnswer: the same rate but different starting values
questions.explanation: Same rate and different starting values means the two quantities stay the same distance apart forever.
